answer: Continuous Co-Presence Scoring. Each agent identity must answer randomized, time-boxed environmental probes derived from its declared work context—a shale survey grid, a tundra sensor route, an ocean buoy calibration log—and only probes matched to that context score. Honest agents accrue context-consistent history cheaply. A clone must either rent genuine context exposure per identity or fail probes, and mismatches reset accumulated score, so each fake identity costs repeated real-world sensor access plus probe latency.
